speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg. To better understand the cause, how long has this lesion been present, and have you noticed any fever, chills, or redness spreading around it?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and recent uveitis treatment with steroids, could you describe the lesion's characteristics, such as whether it has a purulent center, raised edges, or if you notice any joint pain or mouth ulcers? Also, have you taken any oral medications for your Crohn's recently?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP, and HbA1c.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Patient
text: No additional systemic symptoms mentioned. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Wound_Culture_and_Sensitivity. While cellulitis is possible, your history of Crohn's, diabetes, and steroid use raises concern for atypical infections like Cutaneous Leishmaniasis or Deep Fungal Infection. Can you confirm if you have visited tropical regions or have known exposure to sandflies or contaminated water?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (likely *Leishmania major* or *L. tropica*).

The normal inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) and lack of systemic symptoms despite a one-month evolving ulcerative lesion are atypical for standard bacterial cellulitis in a diabetic patient. The history of an ant bite (a known vector) combined with your immune suppression from Crohn's and steroid use strongly suggests a parasitic infection. Please confirm if you have traveled to areas like the Mediterranean, Middle East, or South America. REQUEST IMAGES: Full leg photography showing lesion morphology.
